name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish). The dataset also includes Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for all languages.
license: Public domain (derived from LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data released in the public domain)
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 2020.
rai:dataCollection: Audiobooks were downloaded from LibriVox using LibriVox APIs and data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. Text sources for the audiobooks were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org for English, and various other sources for other languages. Some text extraction involved manual approaches including copying text from browsers, extracting from PDF/EPUB files using pdftotext, and writing HTML parsers for popular domains.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For some languages, text sources for audiobooks were missing due to invalid links or pages redirecting to incorrect pages. For example, all text sources from the spiegel.de domain (accounting for 1/3 of German audio data) were being redirected to invalid pages. Manual searching was performed to find alternate sources for unavailable books.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks (read speech) and corresponding text sources from Project Gutenberg and other online book repositories. The dataset covers 8 languages: English (71,506.79 hours in LibriVox), German (3,287.48 hours), Dutch (2,253.68 hours), Spanish (1,438.41 hours), French (1,333.35 hours), Portuguese (284.59 hours), Italian (279.43 hours), and Polish (137.00 hours).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments based on silence intervals. Numbers in transcripts were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels. Hyphens and apostrophes were handled using heuristics. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering of characters outside valid unicode ranges for each language.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: 1) Audio segmentation: long audio files split into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with TDS Convolutions and ASG loss, splitting at silence intervals. 2) Pseudo label generation: beam-search decoding with 4-gram language model on acoustic models. 3) Text normalization: NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters, filtering of invalid unicode characters. 4) Transcript retrieval: TF-IDF similarity on bigrams to find matching documents, followed by Smith-Waterman alignment; candidate transcripts with WER > 40% between candidate and pseudo label were filtered out. 5) Dataset splitting: no speaker overlap between train/dev/test; speakers balanced by gender; books filtered to avoid overlap with LM training data. 6) Language model books filtered to remove overlap with dev/test sets using edit distance and 5-gram inverted index.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts for development and test sets were human-verified. Human transcribers listened to audio files while reading the generated transcript and corrected clear and obvious errors (e.g., diacritic corrections, missing words, missing apostrophes). Transcripts for training data were generated automatically via pseudo-label generation and transcript retrieval from source text.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcript (GT) and human rated transcript (HRT) was measured for dev and test sets across all 8 languages. Error rates ranged from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev), indicating varying levels of correction needed across languages.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference; TDS Convolutions with ASG loss for acoustic models; 4-gram language model for pseudo label generation via beam-search decoding; TF-IDF similarity on bigrams for document retrieval; Smith-Waterman alignment for transcript matching; SVM with RBF kernel for gender classification; KenLM toolkit for 3-gram and 5-gram language model training; pdftotext for extracting text from PDF/EPUB files; num2words library (considered but not used as primary solution)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is made freely available at http://www.openslr.org. Pretrained models and recipes to train acoustic models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/wav2letter. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender is labeled using a gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel). Speaker identity information is present in the dataset. Audio data used for training in-house acoustic models was completely de-identified.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to open new avenues in ASR and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research by providing a large, freely available multilingual speech corpus. It promotes open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, and can be extended for TTS research.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks, which may not represent conversational or spontaneous speech. English is heavily dominant in LibriVox data. Speaker gender balance is enforced in dev and test sets but not necessarily in training sets (e.g., Dutch training set has 9 male and 31 female speakers). MLS dev and test sets for English are intentionally chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of read speech only, which may limit generalization to conversational or spontaneous speech scenarios. Polish has a high OOV rate of 13.39% in the language model, negatively impacting LM-decoded WER. Some audiobooks could not be included due to missing or invalid text sources. The pseudo-label based transcript retrieval may introduce transcription errors, particularly for numbers. The gender classifier used may not be perfectly accurate across all languages.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems; Text-to-Speech (TTS) research; multilingual speech research; low-resource ASR benchmarking (limited supervision sets of 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 10 hours provided); language model training and evaluation.
